A calmer phone, with clear limits
Guardian sets daily app limits, bedtime and study hours, and a website filter for this phone.
Guardian keeps your rules and usage on this phone. It has no account and no server.
It can see which app is open and for how long.
It can check website domain names on this phone when the filter is on. Allowed lookups go to your network\'s DNS resolver, not to Guardian.
It cannot read messages, photos, passwords, or what you type. It does not use the microphone or camera.

Guardian runs only on this phone. App usage, limits, schedules, blocked sites, and the PIN hash are stored on the device. Guardian has no account, no server, and no ads. It never reads messages, photos, passwords, or what you type. Allowed website lookups go to your network\'s DNS resolver when the filter is on.
This PIN protects every setting. You will need it to change limits or remove Guardian.
There is no PIN reset in this version. Keep this PIN somewhere safe.
Uninstalling Guardian or clearing app data deletes the PIN and all rules. Uninstall protection comes in a later step.

Android asks for each permission separately. You can skip a check and finish it later. That check stays off until you return.
Permission setup is not available in this build yet. Tapping Set up opens an explanation. The Android permission screen comes in a later step.
These checks are still off: App limits and schedules, Website filter, Uninstall protection. You can finish them in Parent settings.
Shows screen time and makes daily limits work.
Shows the pause screen when a limit or schedule applies.
Checks website domains against the block list on this phone.

You can change everything later in Parent settings.

Guardian reads how long apps are in the foreground so it can show screen time and enforce daily limits. It does not read what you do inside apps. Android opens a settings screen where you grant this access.
Android requires a visible notice while Guardian protects the phone. The notice shows whether protection is on and opens the status screen. It does not show app names or personal data.

Guardian uses Accessibility to notice which app is open. When a limit or schedule applies, Guardian shows a pause screen instead. Guardian does not read text on the screen, watch taps, type for you, or control other apps. You can turn this off at any time in Android Settings.

Guardian uses a local VPN to check website domain names against its block list. The check happens on this phone. Guardian does not send your browsing to a Guardian server. Allowed domain lookups go to your network\'s DNS resolver. Guardian does not inspect page content and does not hide your IP address. Android shows a VPN key while the filter runs.
Guardian uses Device Admin so the app cannot be uninstalled without your PIN. It does not wipe the phone, lock the screen, or change your password. You can remove Guardian later with your PIN.
I understand what this permission does.
This build records your choice only. It does not open Android settings yet. Permission setup comes in a later step.
Guardian cannot read app time without Usage access. Daily limits are not being enforced.
No screen time recorded yet today.
Choose an app and set a daily limit. Limits reset at midnight.
Schedules pause apps at set times.
Add bedtime or study hours. Apps pause automatically during a schedule.
Adult sites and your blocked sites can load. App limits and schedules keep working.
No custom sites. Guardian blocks its adult site list.
Some apps and browsers use their own DNS or a direct connection and can bypass the filter. Guardian does not inspect HTTPS traffic and cannot see page content. It does not promise perfect blocking.
Your PIN is saved as a salted hash, not as digits. It stays after a restart.
Uninstalling Guardian or clearing app data deletes the PIN and every rule. There is no cloud backup and no PIN reset in this version. Uninstall protection comes in a later step.
